in_hebrew.name: שִבְעָל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: The Hebrew name Sibeal is derived from the Hebrew word 'שבע' (shiv'ah) which means 'seven'. The suffix 'al' is a common Hebrew suffix meaning 'God'. So Sibeal means 'God is my seven'. This name is not found in the Hebrew Bible.

in_greek.name: Σιβέα
in_greek.long_meaning: The Greek name Sibeal is not found in the Septuagint or New Testament. However, it could be derived from the Greek word 'σεβάω' (sebáō) which means 'to reverence, to worship, to fear'. So Sibeal could mean 'Awe-inspiring' or 'Fear of God'.

in_latin.name: Sibylla
in_latin.long_meaning: The Latin name Sibylla is derived from the Latin word 'sibyllus' which means 'prophetess'. The name Sibylla was given to several ancient prophetesses, including the Sibyls of Delphi and Cumae. However, there is no direct biblical reference to this name.
